Faces Of Nice: 25 Ways To Get Inspired

If these stories don't make you want to pin a race bib on soon, we don't know what will.

  • IRONMAN World Championship Distance

SEPT 2023

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:23
Instaread

In addition to the professional field racing the IRONMAN World Championship in Nice, France this weekend, over 2,200 age-group athletes are registered to compete as they look to be crowned world champion in their respective age-group divisions. Live coverage of the 2023 VinFast IRONMAN World Championship will air on  ironman.com/live beginning with body marking at 5 am CEST/11 pm ET. The professional men's start takes place at 6:50 am CEST. 

Read on for a preview of some of the most inspiring age-group athletes racing in this event. If they don't make you want to pick up a pair of goggles and start training, we don't know what will.

Ryuji Nakagawa: Oldest competitor

  • Age: 79
  • From: Japan
  • At 79 years young, Ryuji will be the oldest male competitor at this year’s VinFast IRONMAN World Championship. 

Nicholas Catullo: Youngest competitor  

  • Age: 18
  • From: Texas, United States
  • Nicholas competed at the Athletic Brewing IRONMAN Lake Placid triathlon in July and it was there that he earned a slot to the 2023 VinFast IRONMAN World Championship in Nice on the same day that his father, Chris, did.
  • Read more about Nicholas and his father here

Michael Collins: Son of IRONMAN founders 

  • Age: 61
  • From: Salem, OR, USA
  • Michael is the son of John and Judy Collins, the couple behind the original IRONMAN in 1978. He competed in his first IRONMAN in 1979, the year after the inaugural race. His parents wouldn’t let him start in 1978 because he had a high school swim meet on race morning.    Michael lives and works in Salem, Oregon and has completed numerous IRONMAN and IRONMAN 70.3 events
  • Read more about Collins' journey here

Gordon Haller: Winner of the first-ever IRONMAN in 1978 

  • Age: 73
  • From: Bella Vista, Arkansas, USA
  • Haller became the first athlete to finish an IRONMAN when he completed the first edition of the iconic race in 1978. The event would evolve into what has become the iconic IRONMAN World Championship. Since then, Gordon has completed 23 IRONMAN races, 18 of which were IRONMAN World Championship races. Gordon has continued to race and coach triathletes over the years and remains an inspiration for all athletes who have ever crossed an IRONMAN finish line. He's also a member of the IRONMAN Hall of Fame.
Image

Cyril De Pistoia: Cancer survivor and transplant athlete returns to his birth city 

  • Age: 35
  • From: LA, USA
  • Cyril is a French triathlete who was born in Nice, and is currently living in Los Angeles, USA.  In 2012, Cyril got diagnosed with a severe case acute leukemia, and was given a very low chance of survival. Chemotherapy worked for a while, but it was not enough, and he was referred to partake in an experimental treatment, radiotherapy and later a bone marrow transplant. He had to relearn how to walk, and was left with damaged lungs amongst other long-term effects. To mark ten years after his transplant, and to honour his dad who died the year before, Cyril completed IRONMAN France Nice last year. Cyril is looking forward to travelling back to his birthplace this year to participate in the IRONMAN World Championship, “This means the world to me. Nice happens to be my birthplace, and competing in an IRONMAN event in Nice has been a dream for a long time.” 

Andreas Niedrig: Junkie to IRONMAN

  • Age: 55
  • From: Oer-Erkenschwick, Germany
  • Andreas Niedrig’s drug career began when he was 12, when he started smoking hashish. Then he went on speed and cocaine, finally becoming addicted to heroin and living 8 months on the road. He financed his drug habit with the usual crimes of a small-time crook. Even his wife and daughters weren’t able to keep him from his destructive habit. More than once he came close to death, even attempting suicide. His wife left him, taking their two daughters. He became hunted by the drug mafia. After hitting rock bottom, Andreas, through sheer force of will, started to change his life. He was 26 when he started running, and after three months completed his first marathon in 2:43, and then did his first Olympic distance triathlon. He did his first IRONMAN in 8:07 hours – an incredible feat for a first-timer. Andreas has written his own book ‘From Junkie to IRONMAN’ and a film has also been created about his life. 

Tyler Johnston: Speed skating firefighter does triathlon to lose weight

  • Age: 42
  • Address: N/A
  • Johnston is a firefighter who got into triathlon to lose weight, and says he became addicted to the sport, instead. He’s also a former National Team Speed Skater.  

Tom Kinneman: Lifetime runner beats throat cancer

  • Age: 71
  • Kinneman has been a runner all his life. He started doing triathlons back in 2008, where he qualified for the IRONMAN 70.3 World Championship in Clearwater, Florida. He’s found himself on national podiums and in Team USA slots several times since then, with multiple IRONMAN 140.6 races under his belt, including the 2018 IRONMAN World Championship where he finished second in his age group. In 2021, he was diagnosed with throat cancer and was forced to push off participating in IRONMAN Florida until the next year. He faced a slow recovery from treatment, but in 2022 he won his age group and ticket to the Vinfast IRONMAN World Championship. 

Adam Melonas: Aussie chef and 'fastfood' founder 
 

  • Age: 42
  • From: Newton, MA
  • Melonas is an Australian chef based in Massachusetts, and founder of sports performance company Chew which has a developed Fastfood which was developed in collaboration with endurance athletes and incorporates galactose, providing a stable supply of carbohydrates. As both a chef and an IRONMAN triathlete, Melonas believes he has an intimate understanding of the essential benefits of quality high-performance fuel. 
Image

Noel Mulkey: Social media star heads to second IRONMAN World Championship  

  • Age: 27
  • Address: Tulsa, OK
  • Noel Mulkey, a Tulsa native, will tell you he is a former overweight drug addict who found a love for triathlon and turned his life around because of it. At his worst, he would regularly spend $500 a day on heroin until checking into a clinic with the support of his family to begin a much-desired recovery. In an effort to lose the weight gained after replacing his substance urges with food, Noel made the decision to begin living a healthier lifestyle. He took up running, even averaging 60 to 70 miles a week which led to the decision to mix it up with swimming and biking. Discovering triathlon, Noel had turned his life around for the better racing multiple IRONMAN 70.3 events, qualifying for the IRONMAN 70.3 World Championship and even finishing his first IRONMAN in Panama City Beach in the fall of 2020. Always open to sharing his experience, Noel continues to document his day-to-day training on social media. After the pandemic hit, he picked up TikTok even amassing over 1.5 million followers while sharing his training routine which often includes waking up at 3:30 a.m., setting off on 60-mile indoor bike rides and four-mile runs — accomplishing all before noon each day. Follow Noel’s journey on TikTok in the link below.  The social media sensation is excited to challenge himself at the IRONMAN World Championship in Nice, France.  

Glen Weissman: How triathlon has shaped one couple's marriage

  • Age: 54
  • Weissman’s first IRONMAN was IRONMAN Canada back in 2011, the same day as his wedding anniversary. He told his wife before he registered that he was going to take her to Hawaii for their anniversary. Then, he explained what that really meant—that he’d virtually be a ghost for the next year while he trained, and that they won’t spend much time together on their actual anniversary. With a few tries, he made good on that promise in 2014, and he’s thrilled to be back this year at the Vinfast IRONMAN World Championship this year. The day of his qualifying event—you guessed it—the same day as their wedding anniversary. 

Antoine Scortarore: The race of a lifetime from military veteran who survived cancer 

  • Age: 27
  • From: France
  • Antoine was in the military, part of the Air Force division. He served in the military for 12 years. Following the announcement in 2018 that he had cancer - immune system (lymphoma). The doctors were pessimistic about his ambitions of racing triathlons, but he was determined and never imagined stopping and giving up on his dream.  He felt that his body would recover and cope through the triathlon lifestyle he was seeking. After the chemotherapy sessions, he continued to run, cycle and train because he felt the need to do so, and he needed to get away from the mundane routine. He now hosts conferences where he encourages those with cancer to not give up on life.   
Image

Pawel Bugajny Hilfiker: Avid 60-year old ultra-runner takes on IRONMAN World Championship

  • Age: 60
  • Address: Poznan, Poland
  • Pawel has finished 6 IRONMAN events on 6 different continents (Africa, Europe, South America, North America, Asia, Australasia). Remarkably he has done all this in a period of just one year. In total, he has finished 19 IRONMAN events globally while also pursuing his main passion of being a mountain climber and ultra runner.  

David Llinares: Full-circle—he first began his triathlon journey in nice in 1999 and will retire this year

  • Age: 51
  • Lives: La Jonquera, Spain
  • David has been a long-distance triathlete since 1999 when he participated in his first ever long-distance triathlon in Nice, France. He has been racing long distance triathlons ever since and is wanting to finish his long age group racing event at a pinnacle event in Nice this year. 

Tom Bill: Former Royal Marine Commando to race in Nice 

  • Age: 32
  • Lives: Stafford, UK
  • ​​​​​​​A Former royal marine commando, Tom will be representing the United Kingdom at the 2023 VinFast IRONMAN World Championship in Nice, France. The ex-marine has taken up the sport of triathlon as a coach and participant.  

Bernhard Schneider: Despite suffering cardiac arrhythmia, athlete pushes on to achieve his dream

  • Age: 65
  • Lives: Rüschlikon, Switzerland
  • Bernhard is adamant to continue living his dream lifestyle of being active and participating in the sport he loves despite all odds. He shares, “Exactly one year after my first ablation because of atrial fibrillation I qualified first time for the 2016 IRONMAN World Championship event in Hawaii. Let’s see how my heart works after my second ablation on 25th January 2023. I had heart surgery in 2016, which minimized the atrial fibrillation, but it's not completely gone. If it comes up today, I'll take it as an indication that I'm overtaxing myself mentally or physically in my current condition, and I'll scale back my performance a bit.” 

Bent Andersen: 6-time age-group IRONMAN World Champion looking for a maiden title in Nice

  • Age: 59
  • ​​​​​​​Address: Herning, Denmark
  • Bent, a warehouse manager, has won his age group six times at the IRONMAN World Championship in Kailua-Kona, Hawaii. He is looking for his seventh World Championship title and relishing the new course in Nice, France to see if he can win on a different course and different weather conditions.  

Elmar Sprink: 9 IRONMAN events and 19 IRONMAN 70.3 events later despite donor heart 

  • Age: 36
  • Lives: Germany
  • Elmar Sprink is considered the fittest heart-transplanted person in the world. For almost nine years, the East Westphalian has been on the road with a donor heart - as a triathlete, trail runner, mountain biker, mountain climber, snowboarder, skier and surfer.

Andreas, Ulrike, and Alexander Torpsch​​​​​​​: “It's a family affair:" Three siblings qualify together for the world championships in Nice and Hawai`i.  

  • Lives: Germany
  • All three siblings have secured a slot for the respective World Championships this year at the Mainova IRONMAN European Championship Frankfurt 2023 (sister for Hawaii and brothers for Nice).
  • Read more of their story here

Marc Clough: Brain surgery won't stop him 

  • Age: 52
  • ​​​​​​​Address: Great Britain
  • Marc has been a fighter since his birth. Born with a brain AVM rupture causing hemorrhaging in his brain, Clough has never let that slow him down. He has completed 9 IRONMAN triathlons even after having a third of his brain removed through two cranial operations. He is excited to finish his 10th IRONMAN competition at this year’s IRONMAN World Championship in Nice.  

Andres Gutierrez: Disabled athlete ready to take on Nice 

  • Age: 41
  • Address: Costa Rica
  • A proud father and husband, Andres takes pride in competing in triathlon at the highest level despite his disability. Andres suffered a bike accident and lost much of the mobility of his left arm and internal and external rotation proving the swim portion even more difficult. He does not let his disability stop him from racing in IRONMAN events and having a successful life.  

Kuo-Chang Hung: Visually impaired athlete takes on Nice

  • Age: 43
  • Lives: Taiwan
  • ​​​​​​​Visually impaired athlete from Taiwan is ready to compete at the IRONMAN World Championship in Nice.  

Sam Lambooy: Young Australian man challenges himself during COVID and falls in love with endurance sports 

  • Age: 27 
  • ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​Lives: Austin, Texas, USA  
  • Pictured at top, Sam Lambooy’s endurance sports journey began in his home country of Australia at the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.  Prior to the COVID lockdown, the furthest Sam had ever run was 14 km. In 2020, Sam worked with a coach and challenged himself to run a sub three-hour marathon in 12 months. Throughout the process, Sam lost 33 pounds, and gained a mental strength he said he didn’t know he had, ‘running became a space where I was able to process feelings of loss and frustration, but also relish feelings of appreciation for my friends and family, as well as gain confidence in my identity and strength.’ In 2021, Sam raced the Hobart marathon in Hobart, Australia, finishing in 2 hours, 58 minutes, and 53 seconds.   Sam’s job moved him to Austin, Texas where he continued his training and in was introduced to IRONMAN Foundation athlete, Tim Deer.  He purchased his first road bike in April, 2022 and completed his first IRONMAN, IRONMAN Chattanooga in 2022 in 10 hours and 59 minutes. Now, Sam has set his sights on raising money for the IRONMAN Foundation and crossing the IRONMAN World Championship finish line in Nice, France with his mentor, Tim Deer.
